help.commands.heading: Commands
help.commands.ignore: Block any messages from the specified user on the current network. This can be a nickname or a hostmask.
help.commands.ignorelist: Load the list of ignored users for the current network.
help.commands.invite: Invite a user to the specified channel. If {channel} is omitted, user will be invited to the current channel.
help.commands.join: Join a channel. Password is only needed in protected channels and can usually be omitted.
help.commands.kick: Kick a user from the current channel.

help.commands.mode: Set the given flags to the current channel if the active window is a channel, another user if the active window is a private message window, or yourself if the current window is a server window.
help.commands.msg: Send a message to the specified channel.
help.commands.mute: Prevent messages from generating any feedback for a channel. This turns off the highlight indicator, hides mentions and inhibits push notifications. Muting a network lobby mutes the entire network. Not specifying any channel target mutes the current channel. Revert with {command}.
help.commands.nick: Change your nickname on the current network.
help.commands.notice: Sends a notice message to the specified channel.
help.commands.op: Give op ({mode}) to one or several users in the current channel.
help.commands.part: Close the specified channel or private message window, or the current channel if {channel} is omitted.
help.commands.query: Send a private message to the specified user.
help.commands.quit: Disconnect from the current network with an optional message.
help.commands.raw: Send a raw message to the current IRC network.
help.commands.rejoin: Leave and immediately rejoin the current channel. Useful to quickly get op from ChanServ in an empty channel, for example.
help.commands.search: Search for messages in the current channel / user
help.commands.slap: Slap someone in the current channel with a trout!
help.commands.topic: Get the topic in the current channel. If {newtopic} is specified, sets the topic in the current channel.
help.commands.unban: Unban ({mode}) a user from the current channel. This can be a nickname or a hostmask.
help.commands.unignore: Unblock messages from the specified user on the current network. This can be a nickname or a hostmask.
help.commands.unmute: Un-mutes the given channel(s) or the current channel if no channel is provided. See {mute} for more information.
help.commands.ver: Ask a user which client they run: a {ctcp} VERSION request, the same as {command}. The answer shows where you asked.
help.commands.voice: Give voice ({mode}) to one or several users in the current channel.
help.commands.who: List who matches the mask (a channel, a nick or a wildcard {mask}), as a table. Without a mask, the users of the current channel.
help.commands.whois: Retrieve information about the given user on the current network.

settings.notifications.keyChangeTrust: Naive — renew it on the spot, without asking
settings.notifications.noHttps: Notifications are only supported over HTTPS connections.
settings.notifications.pushBlocked: The server refused the push subscription. It may require logging in (SASL) before subscribing.
settings.notifications.pushDenied: Notifications are blocked by your browser. Allow them in the browser's site settings, then try again.
settings.notifications.pushDeniedAndroid: Notifications are turned off for this app. Allow them in Android's settings for the app, then try again.
settings.notifications.pushPerNetwork: Push is set up per network — turn it on or off in each network's settings (Edit network → “Push notifications for this network”), where the enrollment status is also shown. The browser delivers the notifications; each push-capable server decides whether to wake this app.
settings.notifications.serverUnsupported: Push notifications need a connected server that supports the draft/webpush capability and you to be logged in to an account.
settings.notifications.stale: A server's push identity (its key) changed, so this device's push subscription for it no longer works. Renew it from that network's settings (Edit network → “Renew push notifications”) to keep being notified while the app is closed.
settings.notifications.unsupported: Push notifications are not supported by this browser (they need the Push API, a service worker and a secure context).
